deep.reconstruction:
This folio is a draft of §§4–5 of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrischen Reihe' (written 1854, published 1867). It restarts the opening of the previous folio, cutting away the convergence discussion so that the concept of the integral can be fixed first.

(0) Setting. Consider the series

 f(x) = ½b_0 + Σ_{n≥1} (a_n sin nx + b_n cos nx).

f is defined only at the points x where the series converges.

(1) Formal Fourier coefficients. Multiply by sin mx dx or cos mx dx and integrate over [−π, π]. Using orthogonality (my filling-in: ∫ sin mx sin nx = π δ_{mn}, ∫ cos mx cos nx = π δ_{mn} for m, n ≥ 1, and ∫ sin mx cos nx = 0), one gets

 a_m = (1/π) ∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) sin mx dx,
 b_m = (1/π) ∫_{−π}^{π} f(x) cos mx dx.

The ½b_0 convention makes the cosine formula valid for m = 0 as well. Riemann notes that this is allowed only if ∫_{−π}^{π} f dx exists. A right-column fragment glosses 'exists' as: a fixed limit exists towards which the sum Σ … converges. He therefore separates two cases:
- Case 1: the integral exists.
- Case 2: no such integral exists.

(2) Section I: what does ∫_a^b f dx mean?
- Choose a partition a < x_1 < … < x_{n−1} < b.
- Set δ_1 = x_1 − a, δ_2 = x_2 − x_1, …, δ_n = b − x_{n−1}.
- Let the ε_i be proper positive fractions, 0 < ε_i < 1.
- Form S = δ_1 f(a + ε_1δ_1) + δ_2 f(x_1 + ε_2δ_2) + … + δ_n f(x_{n−1} + ε_nδ_n).

S depends on the choice of the δ and the ε. If S tends to a fixed limit A as all δ_i → 0, however the δ and ε are chosen, then A is called ∫_a^b f dx. This is the Riemann sum and the Riemann integral. Where S has no limit, the symbol has no meaning under this definition. A crossed-out right-column draft repeats this.

(3) Extension for unbounded integrands. If f becomes infinite on approaching a single point c of [a, b], then S can take any value however small the δ are. Hence ∫_a^b in the above sense does not exist. If, however,

 ∫_a^{c−α_1} f dx + ∫_{c+α_2}^b f dx

tends to a fixed limit as α_1 and α_2 tend to 0 independently, that limit is taken as ∫_a^b f dx. This is the improper integral. Riemann says this extension 'has found general acceptance' and that he will use only it.

He rejects other conventions of Cauchy (implicitly the principal value, α_1 = α_2). They may be useful for particular classes of investigations, but are not generally adopted and are too arbitrary.

(4) Section II, beginning. Let D_1 be the oscillation (Schwankung) of f on [a, x_1], i.e. the difference between its largest and smallest values there, D_2 the oscillation on [x_1, x_2], and so on. The page breaks off here. In the published text this leads to the criterion: f is integrable iff Σ δ_i D_i → 0 as the δ_i → 0. Equivalently, for each σ > 0 the total length of the intervals with D_i > σ can be made arbitrarily small.
errors: Termwise multiplication and integration of a merely pointwise convergent series is not justified by the mere existence of ∫ f dx. Riemann flags the step only as conditional, and in the final text he avoids relying on it, using the second integration F and Riemann's lemmas instead. As written in the draft, the stated condition is insufficient.

The claim that S can take any value if f is unbounded near a point is essentially right: Riemann sums are unbounded because the tag in the interval containing c can be chosen so f is arbitrarily large. It needs |f| unbounded on every neighbourhood intersecting [a, b]; this is fine as stated.
Some sentences are left unfinished or duplicated (e.g. 'Hat diese Summe … die Eigenschaft deren Werth unabhängig von der Wahl'). These are drafting fragments, not mathematical errors.

results.what: Fourier coefficient formulas obtained by termwise integration, with the caveat that the integral must exist
Definition of the definite integral as the limit of tagged sums S = Σ δ_i f(x_{i−1} + ε_iδ_i) as the mesh tends to 0, independent of tags
Extension of the integral to an isolated singularity c via independent limits α_1, α_2 → 0
results.modern_name: Improper integral of the second kind

results.what: Rejection of Cauchy's other conventions (principal value, α_1 = α_2) as arbitrary
Introduction of the oscillation D_i of f on each subinterval
results.modern_name: Oscillation; Riemann's integrability criterion (Σ δ_i D_i → 0)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of §§4–5 of the published Habilitationsschrift (Riemann integral, improper integral, oscillation). The content is well known as Riemann's. Only the drafting variants, such as the explicit 'too arbitrary' verdict on Cauchy's conventions, are of minor philological interest.

checkable.asserts: Riemann sums with tag fraction 1/2 for x^2 on [0,1] tend to 1/3
Improper integral of |x|^(-1/2) over [-1,1] with independent limits exists and equals 4
For 1/x on [-1,2] the two-sided sum is log2 + log(a1/a2): no limit for independent a1, a2 (improper integral fails), but the Cauchy principal value (a1 = a2) gives log 2

transcription_corrections: Line 2: the struck word at left before the series appears to be 'ferner' (deleted); the first line reads 'Wir beschäftigen uns mit der Reihe'.

The right-column insertion after 'wenn ∫_{-π}^{π} f x dx' reads roughly 'd. h. ein fester Grenzwerth existirt, gegen welchen Σ … convergirt'. The marginal formula is the Riemann sum Σ(δ_1 f(a+ε_1δ_1) + … + δ_n f(x_{n-1}+ε_nδ_n)), partly struck.
In the definition, 'b − x_{n−1} durch δ_n' is intended where the transcription has '… b − x_{n-1} [?]'.
The '39' at top right is the folio number, not mathematics.

In the Cauchy paragraph, 'zweckmäßig sein … sie sind indeß nicht allgemein eingeführt und dazu, schon wegen ihrer großen Willkürlichkeit' is the main reading. The phrase 'zu willkürlich' in the transcription is uncertain.
